# gezor_sso_provider (Resource)

An OpenID Connect single sign-on provider for a workspace.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "gezor_sso_provider" "entra" {
  kind            = "entra"
  display_name    = "Acme Entra ID"
  entra_tenant_id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
  client_id       = var.entra_client_id
  client_secret   = var.entra_client_secret
  status          = "active"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `kind` (String) `entra`, `okta` or `google`. One provider of each kind per workspace.

### Optional

- `client_id` (String)
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) Client secret. Write-only: it is never read back, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected.
- `cloud` (String) Entra cloud: `global`, `usgov`, `china` or `germany`.
- `display_name` (String) Name on the sign-in button.
- `entra_tenant_id` (String) Microsoft Entra tenant id.
- `group_claim` (String) ID token claim that lists groups.
- `issuer` (String) OIDC issuer URL. Derived for Google and for Entra when `entra_tenant_id` is set.
- `status` (String) `disabled`, `ready` or `active`. `active` needs issuer, client id and client secret.
- `workspace` (String) Workspace id or slug. Defaults to the provider's `workspace`. Changing it recreates the resource.

### Read-Only

- `has_client_secret` (Boolean)
- `id` (String) Provider id.
- `redirect_uri` (String) Callback URL to register with the identity provider.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Append @<workspace> to import from a workspace other than the provider default.
terraform import gezor_sso_provider.example <provider_id>
```
